bp-mariano-2024.title: Jack Mariano (Pasco County Board of Commissioners District 5, Florida, candidate 2024)

promises.value: Why running: "We need leaders more concerned about creating jobs than protecting their own."
Priority on taxes: said it is imperative to stimulate the local economy by reducing taxes on citizens and businesses; said the Penny for Pasco sales tax distributes the burden equally
Priority on county leadership: called for a nationwide search for a new county administrator with experience in a county of 750,000 to 1,000,000 people
Priority on mobility fees: said he did not understand replacing impact fees with mobility fees, which he said do not cover the entire cost of infrastructure
Supported pursuing the Ridge Road extension: "I think the problem we've had in east Pasco is we need more than two-lane roads"
On paying for storm water drainage: "Assessment is fine. Everyone has storm water."
Said the mobility fee formula should change so rural and urban areas pay the same rate; said he did not favor increasing school impact fees
On expanding the tax base: "Pasco County has to get more friendly and realize they are in a service position"
When filing for the 2016 race, named flooding, redevelopment and transportation as top issues facing the county

2024 campaign site: "If you want a no-nonsense leader who actually understands the issues facing Pasco County, look no further. I'm not here for recognition; I'm here to get the job done." Site lists "A Commonsense Vision For Our Future" without further policy detail in the archived copy

electionHistory.value: 2012 Republican primary: Lost County Commission District 1 with 31.29%; Ted Schrader won with 37.49%, Rachel O'Connor 31.22%
2016 Republican primary: Won County Commission District 1, 40.29% over Debbie Wells 32.72% and Rachel O'Connor 26.98%
2016 general: Won County Commission District 1, 69.27% over Dimitri A. Delgado (NPA) 30.35%, with write-in votes
2020: No District 1 contest appears on the Nov 2020 general results page
2024 general: Won County Commission District 1, 59.56% to 40.44% over Lisa Moretti (NPA)
2020: Re-elected to District 1 without a vote after opponent Christopher King withdrew
2024: News report says this is Oakley's third term; first elected in 2016
2012: Spent $176,000 of his own money in the 2012 primary, which he lost to incumbent Ted Schrader; said he did not plan to do so again in 2016

keyPositions.value: Supported an apartment request in Jan 2021: "I think the project fits"
As chairman, voted yes as the board approved an apartment request 3-2 (Apr 2021)
Voted against a gas station land use change, which failed 2-3 (Apr 2021)
Seconded the motion to deny the Seven Oaks apartments, saying the development was too big for the site (Jan 2022)
As chairman, voted for higher school impact fees (2024), citing demand for schools from new residents
On the Live Local Act (Jan 2024): "you'd think Live Local is for affordable housing and it's not at all affordable"
Changed his vote to approve the revised Seven Oaks project (Nov 2022) after voting against it in January, saying "It's a better fit on the site than it was prior"
Said the county needs more ball fields but "we can't build more parks without having the money to maintain them" (May 2025)
Said a proposed solar farm site on Blanton Road with nearby transmission lines seemed suitable, while solar would not work on all farmland (Jun 2018)
On paving assessments (Dec 2022): "We've got growing pains and we need our roads repaired"
As chairman (2024), said most new Pasco homes cost $300,000 to $500,000 and many people moving for jobs cannot afford them

financialDisclosures.value: 2025 filing lists organizations: Pasco County Elected Constitutional Officer, Pasco County MPO, Tampa Bay Water Board of Directors.

promises.value: At a 2022 Greater Pasco Chamber forum, spoke about the county's continued development and his hope for its future: "Pasco is on the forefront of tremendous growth"

2022 campaign (as summarized from his website): said he would work to strengthen the local economy, invest in sustainable infrastructure, promote public safety and "preserve Pasco's identity with smart growth"
2022 campaign website, as cited: described himself as a "common sense leader" and said he voted to cut taxes twice on the SWFWMD board
Campaign site (archived Mar 2025) lists issues: "Strengthen Our Local Economy," "Invest In Sustainable Infrastructure," "Promote Public Safety," "Preserving Pasco's Identity With Smart Growth"

electionHistory.value: 2020 general: Lost Mosquito Control Commissioner Seat 1, 33.49% to 66.51% for Randy Evans
2022 Republican primary: Won County Commission District 2, 48.87% over Christie Zimmer 27.11% and Troy F. Stevenson 24.02%. No District 2 contest appears on the Nov 2022 general results page.
2022: After the primary, news report said Weightman would face write-in candidate Louie Rodriguez in November
2026: On the Nov 3, 2026 general election ballot for District 2 against Stephanie C. Vazquez (D); had not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey as of Oct 27, 2026

keyPositions.value: Cast the only vote against higher school impact fees (2024): "I'm concerned with our fee structure that it's going to erode away the opportunity of home ownership for folks"
Championed an additional senior property tax exemption during budget hearings and said he supports the maximum exemption (Oct 2023)
Supported sending the Saddlebrook plan to state review but said he was not overly enthusiastic about its multifamily units or density (Apr 2023)
Raised concerns that data center moratorium language could leave loopholes (Jun 2026)
Advocated a cap exemption for Heritage trees in the tree ordinance approved unanimously (Apr 2026): "You can't mitigate the destruction of Heritage trees"
Criticized state House Bill 399 (2026): "It erodes the ability for local planning commissioners to have a say"
Said sidewalk appropriation requests are his legislative ask every session; the state approved $1.5 million for sidewalks on Wells Rd. and Curley Rd. (2025)
Led Pasco's push to change the state Live Local Act in 2024: "Live Local just did not seem to accomplish that goal"; the board voted 5-0 to opt out of its tax portion
Said the county should revisit diverting Connected City funds to the Villages of Pasadena Hills Superpark (May 2025)
Opposed a requested park impact fee exemption for affordable housing (Aug 2023) "until we understand the full impacts of the Live Local Act"

financialDisclosures.value: Earlier Form 1 filings: 2015 (Public Service Commission Nominating Council) on 6/20/2016; 2016 and 2017 (CareerSource Pasco-Hernando board and PSC Nominating Council) on 6/19/2017 and 8/7/2018; 2019, 2020 and 2021 (Southwest Florida Water Management District Governing Board) on 6/4/2020, 6/17/2021 and 6/16/2022.

conflicts.value: Residency: The Times reported (Aug 18, 2026) that Weightman "faced backlash because he previously didn't live in his commission district" and that he moved into the district two months after he was elected

promises.value: 2004 School Board District 4 race: proposed seeking corporate sponsorship to build a Pasco version of Largo's Enterprise Village for elementary students
Said the district should consider a magnet school or other alternatives for academically advanced children
Wanted greater environmental awareness in the curriculum, expanding teaching space at the Energy and Marine Center and the SWFWMD facility at Starkey Wilderness Park
Wanted school green space and athletic fields more accessible to the public
Priority 1: "Provide incentives for new and existing businesses to create jobs in our community"; said she would devote time to analyzing the county's permit approval process to find solutions
Priority 2: "Reduce our county budget and eliminate wasteful programs," in part by increasing technology and improving workflow
Priority 3: "Protect our county's natural resources and pristine environment"; said the county should continue protecting environmentally sensitive lands from development
2012 campaign site: said her run was prompted by retirements of key county figures: "Maybe my background and experiences and leadership could be of value to the board and the community"

Said she supports continuing the Penny for Pasco sales tax and defended the current mix of projects it funds; named environmentally sensitive lands preservation, transportation projects and economic development as important areas for future county spending (2020 forum)

Said the county is already acquiring green areas and offering rural designations and wildlife corridor protections, while providing room for residential and business growth: "We're growing in a good way"

School Board: campaign site (2012) says she was elected to the School Board in 2004 and served until 2010

keyPositions.value: On a proposed campaign civility pledge (Jan 2020): "I would just say I have no objections to sign anything that says civility and good behavior should be in order." Added: "It doesn't inhibit anyone's free speech."
Said an apartment site was suitable (Jan 2021): "I'm not sure this area is overbuilt for this price point"
Voted yes as the board approved an apartment request 3-2 (Apr 2021); said she wanted evidence the area was oversaturated with apartments
Moved to approve a gas station land use change (Apr 2021); motion failed 2-3
Voted against denial as the board rejected the Seven Oaks apartments (Jan 2022)
Voted for higher school impact fees (2024), saying Pasco's cost of living is "still very affordable" compared with other counties
Said the state Live Local Act benefits institutional investors rather than local developers; met with Senate President Passidomo on it (Jan 2024)

conflicts.value: Ethics complaint dismissed: The Florida Commission on Ethics, meeting June 9, 2023, dismissed a complaint against "KATHRYN STARKEY, Pasco County Commission" for lack of legal sufficiency.
Ethics complaint dismissed: The Commission, meeting July 28, 2023, dismissed a complaint against "KATHY STARKEY, Pasco County Commission Member" for lack of legal sufficiency

promises.value: 2024 campaign site "Pasco Priorities": keep taxes low to combat inflation; grow smarter, not faster; back first responders to improve public safety; protect farmers and ranchers; invest in road and infrastructure improvements; streamline county government
Candidate questionnaire: named "cutting taxes, keeping our streets safe, and ensuring growth is smart and sustainable" as top priorities
Said growth should put "our people first," balancing new development with traffic, infrastructure and quality of life
Said she has made revitalizing the Moon Lake community "a personal mission"

Listed as her record: cutting taxes, advancing economic development, partnering with the Sheriff, expanding recreation, and helping lead debris removal (more than 200 tons) after Hurricanes Helene and Milton (candidate's own description)

Said her guiding principles are "lowering taxes, protecting our quality of life from unchecked growth, strengthening our community against flooding and storms and creating opportunities for our children and families to thrive"
On development: "Development is happening fast, too fast in many cases"; said growth should be smart and consider future needs

Listed as accomplishments: hurricane response, senior food programs, Pasco's first low-barrier homeless shelter, Moon Lake revitalization, a tax rate rollback she said she fought for, and economic development projects such as Moffitt's Speros campus (candidate's own description)

promises.value: Plans to strengthen local teacher pipelines through partnerships with the USF College of Education, PHSC and alternative certification programs; listed AI threat detection, bus driver recruitment and curriculum oversight as priorities

On book challenges (Florida Public Media Voter Guide, as quoted by WUSF): "Book challenges should be handled through a clear, lawful process that respects parents' rights and age-appropriate standards"
Named budget transparency and teacher retention as key issues: "We have to be able to find the money to pay the teachers without an additional tax"
Said she would look into the cost of district health insurance for teachers' family plans
On safety: said the least expensive step is a culture of communication so students report concerns; supports retrofitting single-point entry and mentioned AI weapons-detection technology and cameras
Said she is "a big proponent of school choice" and that "I think it brings excellence and competition"
On the teacher pay referendum: said she is sharing others' social media posts about it and that, if it is taken away, teachers, janitors and bus drivers would suffer

First-year plan: increase career education paths and expand partnerships with community organizations; suggested converting schools with declining enrollment into Junior Achievement-type facilities for certifications and apprenticeships
Said she is running on "putting paper back in the classroom," saying handwriting is important and "nothing can replace teacher interaction"
